original_question: Construct a Khovanov complex for arbitrary virtual-knot diagrams over the integers, understand the existing constructions that work for large classes of virtual links, and determine structural consequences such as which knots are K-full or Kho-full, whether optimal diagrams are minimal in classical crossing number, and which diagram moves preserve that optimality.
target_in_paper: Section 8.1, Problem 13 ("Khovanov homology"), with Problem 29 supplying the paper's more precise technical formulation of the integral-coefficient obstruction.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly captures the main thrust of the paper's Khovanov-homology problem: extend the Khovanov complex to arbitrary virtual diagrams over the integers, account for the existing construction that works for a large class of virtual links, and include the paper's follow-up structural questions about K-full/Kho-full knots, minimality of optimal diagrams, and moves preserving optimality.
missing_details: The paper's existing integer-valued construction is not stated abstractly as applying to 'large classes' in general; it is tied specifically to the orientable atom condition.

The official formulation is for a generalization of the Khovanov complex for arbitrary virtual diagrams, while the known construction discussed there gives Khovanov homology over Z for large classes of virtual links satisfying the orientable-atom hypothesis.
The draft does not define K-full: a virtual knot is K-full if it has a diagram for which the leading term, the lowest term, or both come from the B-state in the Kauffman-bracket sense.
The draft does not define Kho-full: it is the analogous notion relative to the Khovanov invariant.
The draft does not define 'optimal diagrams': these are precisely the diagrams witnessing the K-full or Kho-full property.

The paper also asks a sharper classical-versus-virtual minimality question: if a classical knot K has a minimal classical diagram with n crossings, must every virtual diagram of K have at least n classical crossings?

The paper includes an additional subquestion omitted from the draft: whether any virtual knot can have torsion in the B-state of the Khovanov homology, using the formulation of Khovanov homology in [169, 171].

Problem 29 makes explicit the technical obstruction over Z that your draft leaves implicit: unlike the mod 2 case, a virtual state curve may resmooth to a single curve, and this must be handled in any integral theory.

Problem 29 also asks to clarify Manturov's integral construction in terms closer to Khovanov's original definition; your draft mentions 'understand the existing constructions' but not this specific goal.

No extra polynomial variables, homogeneity assumptions, degree restrictions, or nilpotency conditions occur in the target problem; the hidden assumptions instead concern coefficients, B-state terminology, and the orientable-atom condition.
refined_question: Construct, in the sense of Khovanov's original definition, a Khovanov complex over the ring of integers for arbitrary virtual-knot diagrams, extending and clarifying the orientable-atom-based construction of [169, 171] for large classes of virtual links and resolving the integral-coefficient difficulty caused by virtual state curves that can resmooth to a single curve; then, within this framework, classify K-full virtual knots (those admitting a diagram whose leading term, lowest term, or both come from the B-state) and Kho-full virtual knots (defined analogously for the Khovanov invariant), determine whether such optimal diagrams are always minimal in the number of classical crossings, classify the diagram moves that preserve optimality, decide whether a classical knot with a minimal n-crossing classical diagram can admit any virtual diagram with fewer than n classical crossings, and determine whether the B-state Khovanov homology can contain torsion.
justification: The draft is closest to Section 8.1, Problem 13, because that is the only official problem in the paper that combines: (i) constructing a Khovanov complex for arbitrary virtual diagrams, (ii) the existing orientable-atom construction over Z for large classes of virtual links, and (iii) the K-full/Kho-full, optimality, and minimal-crossing questions. Problem 29 then gives the paper's sharper technical explanation of why the integer-coefficient case is hard and explicitly asks for a reformulation that clarifies Manturov's construction. Section 4 supplies the hidden hypothesis behind the existing construction, namely the orientable-atom condition. There is no relevant Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 1.2, or Theorem 1.3 in this paper for this draft; the relevant target is the open-problem list in Section 8.1.
